title: Cube and Checkerboard Illusions
content: The dark square marked “A” is painted with the identical mixture as the light square marked “B”. (Link to video on Facebook.)The square marked “A” is painted with the identical color mixture as the square marked “B”. Both are a neutral gray. (Link to video.)The lesson from both of these diagrams is that our visual system uses context cues to override the raw information that our eyes receive. It's good to keep this rule in mind when estimating the value and the color of objects.David Briggs, an expert on color theory, did this lecture on color constancy and painting.
